newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SPT rally nudges Prague PX50 higher to 505 points.
newsitem.headline: SPT rally nudges Prague PX50 higher to 505 points.

text.p: The effects of recent flooding in the Czech Republic continued to hamper the Prague Stock Exchange on Thursday, but a late rally in the largest issue, SPT Telecom, let the PX50 index close with a tiny gain.
The Reuter Prague RPIX of 11 blue-chip issues still closed 3.5 points lower than Wednesday, at 1,035.4.

But the broader PX50 was buoyed by the relative weighting of SPT -- which gained 15 crowns to 3,615 after losing 15 at the daily fixing -- sending the exchange's 50-share index up 0.1 points to 505.0.
Analysts say the market is still suffering from broad economic worries about last week's devastating floods in the eastern third of the country.

"The biggest problem seems that the infrastructure is disrupted and it will take some time to organise (transport) and this will cause problems for the big companies," said Jindrich Weiss, analyst at Zivnostenska Banka.
SPT, the fixed-line monopoly which says it will suffer losses in the "hundreds of millions of crowns" because of the flooding, has said that its troubles in the flood area are manageable.

The country's largest bank Komercni Banka lost 45 crowns to 1,695, and CEZ power, which is also expected to take at least some hit from the flooding due to lower demand for electricity, was down 12 crowns to 906.

On the PSE's main and parallel markets, 127 issues advanced, 85 declined, and 49 were unchanged. Overall turnover in automated and direct trades registered at the PSE was 813.4 million crowns on a volume of 598,547 shares changing hands.

Komercni's chief economist Kamil Janacek forecast on Thursday that because of the flooding, Czech real gross domestic product growth should come in for the whole of 1997 at the low end of the bank's 1.5 to 2.5 percent range.

The unsure outlook for the economy has become a drag on the already battered share market. Construction issues had posted gains on the prospects of the reconstruction in the flooded area in recent days, but ran out of steam on Thursday.
Construction group IPS Praha gained eight crowns to 218, but Vodni Stavby lost 10 to 909 and Armabeton lost 9.26 crowns to 175.99.
"There is still demand for (construction) shares," Weiss said.
